correctness.rationale: Reconstructed each sign and normalization from Ma Theorem 2.3 and the finite-support right inverse. For every order the r=0 weighted functional is unbounded, while all r>=1 forms are bounded on the R-completion. A tail-supported correction proves the positive r=0 term has no effect on the infimum; a growing weighted v0 witness forces -infinity when alpha<0. Polar decomposition identifies the exact bottom eigenvalue of the (m-1)-dimensional Gram form, including the zero spectral branch. For m=2 partial fractions, digamma recurrence and incompatible equality conditions yield the explicit value and nonattainment. Exact rational Gram checks for m<=4 and both signs of alpha supplement but do not prove the universal theorem. No unproved finite-to-infinite inference is used.

Residual risk remains that the density argument is implicit elsewhere.

value.rationale: The canonical weighted commutator coefficient quantifies the strength of hyponormality of a recently resolved all-order Cesaro family. The theorem solves the full integer-order infinite-dimensional optimization by an exact finite Hermitian matrix, not just the previously known 1/36 lower bound or c=1 threshold. The second-order digamma specialization yields a sharp, naturally parameterized nonattained coefficient; the weighted-kernel density mechanism is reusable for other singular positive-rank perturbations. The result is not an arbitrary finite slice or a known-table recomputation.
